plan.contextChunk: This figure shows a single right triangle drawn in plain black outline with no axes, grid, or shading. The triangle sits on a horizontal base labeled a beneath its midpoint. From the right end of that base a vertical side rises, labeled p on its outer edge. The hypotenuse slants down from the top of the vertical side to the left vertex, labeled h above its middle. A small open square at the lower right vertex marks the right angle between the base and the vertical side, and a single arc at the left vertex marks the acute angle, labeled with the Greek letter theta. The labeling is organized around theta rather than around the page: a is adjacent to theta, p is opposite it, and h is the hypotenuse, so each name states a role rather than a direction. Carrying no numbers at all, the drawing serves as the reference diagram for recovering an unknown acute angle from two known side lengths, the given pair determining which inverse trigonometric relation applies.

interactionPlan.concept: In a right triangle, the names adjacent, opposite, and hypotenuse are roles defined relative to a chosen acute angle θ, and any two of those side lengths determine θ through an inverse trigonometric relation.
elements: Right triangle in plain black outline, no axes or grid
Horizontal base side from left vertex to lower-right vertex, labeled 'a' in italic below its midpoint
Vertical side rising from the lower-right vertex to the apex, labeled 'p' in italic to the right of its midpoint
Hypotenuse slanting from the apex down to the left vertex, labeled 'h' in italic above its midpoint
Small open square at the lower-right vertex marking the 90° angle
Single arc at the left vertex marking the acute angle, labeled with Greek letter 'θ'
Role caption area (appears on click): text such as 'a — adjacent to θ', 'p — opposite θ', 'h — hypotenuse'
Readout showing current θ in degrees and the three ratios p/h, a/h, p/a
Highlight styling: selected side drawn thick in accent color with θ arc echoing the same color
Relation banner showing the matching inverse form, e.g. θ = sin⁻¹(p/h), θ = cos⁻¹(a/h), θ = tan⁻¹(p/a)

interactions.teaches: Each side name states a role relative to θ — clicking a, p, or h highlights that side together with the θ arc and names it adjacent, opposite, or hypotenuse, rather than left, up, or slanted.
Changing the acute angle reshapes the triangle while the labels keep their roles: as θ grows, the opposite side p lengthens relative to the adjacent side a, so the ratio p/a encodes the angle.
interactions.label: Acute angle θ (degrees)

interactions.teaches: Which two side lengths are known decides which inverse relation recovers θ — entering a ratio of sides sets the triangle's shape and lights up the matching sine, cosine, or tangent inverse.
interactions.label: Enter a known side ratio

fields.label: ratio =
fields.role: ratio selector — which pair of sides is known

fields.label: value =
fields.role: numeric value of that ratio, used to solve for θ

demo_steps.title: The reference triangle
demo_steps.narration: A bare right triangle: base a, vertical side p, hypotenuse h, a square marking the right angle and an arc marking the acute angle θ. There are no numbers — this is a template, not a specific triangle.

demo_steps.title: Names are roles, not directions
demo_steps.narration: Click each label in turn. a lies against θ, so it is adjacent; p sits across from θ, so it is opposite; h stretches between them as the hypotenuse. Move θ to the other vertex in your mind and the names would swap.

demo_steps.title: Shallow angle
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ down to about 20°. The opposite side p becomes short compared with the adjacent side a, so p/a is small — a small ratio means a small angle.

demo_steps.title: Steep angle
demo_steps.narration: Push θ up to about 70°. Now p towers over a and the ratio p/a is large. Every value of θ gives one distinct set of ratios.

demo_steps.title: Running it backwards
demo_steps.narration: Type a known ratio — say p/h = 0.5 — and the triangle snaps to the angle that produces it, with θ = sin⁻¹(0.5) highlighted. Two measured sides are enough to recover the unknown angle.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Adjacent, opposite, and hypotenuse are roles assigned by θ, not fixed directions on the page — and because each angle produces its own unique set of side ratios, reading a ratio backwards through an inverse trig function recovers the angle.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Center a single black-outline right triangle on a white field: a long horizontal base, a shorter vertical right side, and a hypotenuse falling from the apex to the sharp left vertex, so the triangle is wide and low. Italic serif labels: 'a' centered below the base, 'p' outside the vertical side, 'h' above the midpoint of the hypotenuse, 'θ' just inside the left vertex next to a single thin arc. A small open square at the lower-right vertex marks the right angle. No axes, no grid, no shading, no numbers in the default view. On interaction, the selected side and the θ arc turn a single accent color (e.g. orange for opposite, blue for adjacent, green for hypotenuse) with a short caption naming its role; a small side panel shows θ in degrees and the three ratios, and a banner shows the matching inverse relation. When θ changes, keep the hypotenuse length fixed and the left vertex anchored so the triangle visibly rocks between wide-and-flat and narrow-and-tall while the labels stay attached to their sides.

Given two sides of a right triangle like the one shown in the figure, find an angle.

An illustration of a right triangle with an angle theta. Adjacent to theta is the side a, opposite theta is the side p, and the hypoteneuse is side h.

discrepancies: Composition: the triangle sits low and left inside the 560×300 viewbox (base spans only x≈140–337, apex near y≈138), leaving a large empty band on the right and top, whereas the source triangle is centred and fills most of the frame — the generated figure reads noticeably smaller and off-centre.
The right-angle marker is drawn as an open two-segment corner path; the source shows a complete small closed square at the right angle.

The source's hypotenuse/base stroke weight is uniformly thin black; the generated default is similar but selection turns entire sides into thick coloured strokes (blue/orange/green) not present in the source — acceptable as interaction state but it departs from the all-black original once used.

Source hypotenuse rises to a slightly steeper apparent slope with a longer base relative to height; at the default θ=30° the proportions are close but the triangle is scaled down relative to the frame.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, correctly labelled reproduction of the bare right-triangle template with an unusually rich and pedagogically sound interaction set (θ slider, side-role selection with popups, demo steps, inverse-ratio solver); the main weakness is layout — the triangle is small and off-centre in the canvas with large empty margins, and the right-angle marker is open rather than a closed square.
action_items: Centre and enlarge the triangle within the viewbox (e.g. recompute Vx/By/L per θ so the figure is roughly centred and fills ~80% of the frame) to match the source's framing.
Draw the right-angle marker as a closed small square (add the fourth edge or use a rect) to match the source glyph.
Suppress the automatic showPopup on every side click (make it a secondary 'explain' affordance) so repeated clicking does not obscure the figure; the inline role caption alone suffices.
Keep default-state strokes strictly black/thin so step 0 is a pixel-level drop-in for the static source, applying colour only as a transient highlight.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are sound (no failure modes, concept_accuracy 5); remaining issues are concrete implementation fixes — centering/scaling the triangle, closing the right-angle square, popup behavior, and default stroke styling.

discrepancies: Source triangle is slightly steeper (apex angle ≈34°) than the default 30° state, and the generated drawing is scaled to fill the frame with slightly thinner strokes — a cosmetic difference only.
An extra on-canvas role caption (e.g. 'a — adjacent to θ') is drawn in the upper-left after a side is selected; not present in the source, though it is absent in the default step-0 state.
The 'p' label sits slightly further from the vertical side than in the source, and the right-angle square is drawn a touch smaller relative to the triangle.
evaluation.notes: A clean, faithful reproduction of the bare right-triangle template (a, p, h, right-angle square, θ arc) with correct serif-italic labels, backed by genuinely useful interactions — θ slider, side-role highlighting with explanations, demo steps, and an inverse-ratio solver; only trivial cosmetic differences from the source.
action_items: Set the default θ closer to the source's ~34° so the step-0 render is a pixel-level drop-in for the static image.
Keep the on-canvas role caption confined to a fixed, clearly-empty corner (or move it entirely into the side panel) so it can never crowd the hypotenuse at steep θ.
Clamp/flag the solver result honestly: when findRoot returns an angle outside the 5–85° slider range, say so rather than silently snapping θ to the clamp and showing a mismatched ratio.

feedback.rationale: All criteria scored 5 with no failure modes and only trivial cosmetic differences noted, so further iteration is unnecessary.
